{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgDZtktF9rpgzVzrmu5t6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT ANALYSIS.md ===\n# Blueprint Analysis: drydock Layers Testing Uat Case\n\n## Commander Expectations\n\n- assert the product is a command-line cash ledger, delivered as an executable named `ledger` at the application root\n- assert every command either completes in full or changes nothing\n- assert every report is computed from the database and never embeds a known answer\n- assert the supplied `sources/run.sh` grader exits zero unmodified against the completed application\n- assert all database access goes through the shipped persistence library, selected by `DATABASE_URL`\n- assert amounts are stored as integer cents and printed with exactly two decimal places\n- assert no account balance ever goes negative\n- assert the application provides a POSIX `bin/test.sh` whose automated suite passes\n\n## Crew\n\n| Crew | Charge |\n|---|---|\n| Commander | Defines intent and decides what done means. |\n| Team Lead | Confirms epic completeness and stakeholder expectations. |\n| Planning Crew | Authors atomic specifications and the ordered Manifest. |\n| Shipyard Crew | Builds the tickets without synchronous Commander access. |\n\n## Story List\n\n### Feature: Command Line Interface\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| CLI-001 | Dispatch commands and reject usage errors | Unknown command, unknown table, unknown report, or wrong argument count exits 2 with one stderr line and nothing on stdout. |\n| CLI-002 | Provide per-command help text | Every command and sub-verb in the Commands table has one line of help text, printed in the usage diagnostic on stderr. |\n| CLI-003 | Emit the CSV success output contract | Every successful command except `init` writes a header row then data rows, comma-separated, unquoted, `\\n` endings, no trailing spaces; `init` writes nothing. |\n\n### Feature: Database Access\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| DB-001 | Resolve the database location | `DATABASE_URL`, then `DATABASE_PATH`, then `data/app.db` is used; an optional `sqlite://` prefix is accepted; a `postgres://` or `postgresql://` value is recognized and fails with exit 1 in this build. |\n| DB-002 | Report unreachable database, missing tables, or unreadable files | Database unreachable, tables missing for a non-`init` command, or an unreadable input file exits 1 with no change. |\n| DB-003 | Run every command in one database transaction | Each command runs in one transaction; any failure rolls back all changes; a write lock held by another connection exits 1 with no change. |\n| DB-004 | Enforce the non-negative balance rule before commit | Any command that would leave an account touched by its changes below zero exits 3 with no change. |\n\n### Feature: Schema Lifecycle\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| SCHEMA-001 | Initialize an empty schema | `ledger init` drops the three tables if present, recreates them empty, writes nothing, and exits 0. |\n| SCHEMA-002 | Count rows per table | `ledger count` prints `table,rows` then `accounts`, `categories`, `transactions` counts in that order. |\n\n### Feature: Field Validation\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| VAL-001 | Validate codes, names, descriptions, and memos | Codes are 1 to 12 characters of `A-Z` and `0-9`; names and descriptions are 1 to 40 characters; memos are 0 to 60; none contains a comma or newline; violations exit 3. |\n| VAL-002 | Parse and format amounts | Input matches `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`, is nonzero, and is stored as integer cents; output has two decimals, a leading `-` when negative, and no separators. |\n| VAL-003 | Validate calendar dates | Dates are real `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar dates; impossible dates such as `2026-02-30` exit 3. |\n\n### Feature: Bulk Loading\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| LOAD-001 | Load the accounts file | `load accounts <csv>` checks the header, validates each row, rejects duplicate keys, stores all or none, and prints `table,loaded` and `accounts,<rows>`. |\n| LOAD-002 | Load the categories file | `load categories <csv>` follows the same header, validation, duplicate, and atomicity contract as accounts. |\n| LOAD-003 | Load the transactions file | `load transactions <csv>` keeps each file `txn_id`, rejects unknown accounts or categories and any balance breach for the whole file, and stores none of the rows on rejection. |\n\n### Feature: Account Maintenance\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| ACCT-001 | Add an account | `account add` prints the new row with `0` transactions and `0.00` balance; a duplicate code exits 3. |\n| ACCT-002 | Get an account | `account get` prints the row with transaction count and balance; an absent code exits 4. |\n| ACCT-003 | Rename an account | `account rename` prints the updated row; an absent code exits 4; an invalid name exits 3. |\n| ACCT-004 | Delete an account | `account delete` prints `deleted` and the code when no transactions reference it; an in-use account exits 3; an absent account exits 4. |\n\n### Feature: Transaction Maintenance\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| TXN-001 | Post a transaction | `txn post` assigns the next id, validates all fields, checks that the account and category exist, applies the balance rule, and prints the new row. |\n| TXN-002 | Get a transaction | `txn get` prints the row; an absent id exits 4; a non-integer id exits 3. |\n| TXN-003 | Amend a transaction amount | `txn amend` changes only the amount, prints the updated row, applies the balance rule, and exits 4 for an absent id. |\n| TXN-004 | Delete a transaction | `txn delete` prints `deleted` and the id, applies the balance rule, and exits 4 for an absent id. |\n\n### Feature: Transfers\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| XFER-001 | Transfer between two accounts | `transfer` stores two `TRANSFER` rows with the next two ids and the stated memos, or neither; requires a positive amount, distinct accounts, and existing accounts; applies the balance rule. |\n\n### Feature: Reports\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| RPT-001 | Balances report | `report balances` prints one row per account ordered by code, then the `TOTAL` row. |\n| RPT-002 | Categories report | `report categories` prints every category ordered by code, including those with no transactions, then the `TOTAL` row. |\n| RPT-003 | Monthly report | `report monthly` prints one row per `YYYY-MM` that has transactions, ascending, then the `TOTAL` row. |\n\n### Feature: Verification and Acceptance\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| VER-001 | Provide the `bin/test.sh` automated suite | `bin/test.sh` is POSIX `sh`, drives the pytest suite against a real temporary database, and exits zero only when every test passes. |\n| VER-002 | Pass the supplied acceptance grader end to end | `sh sources/run.sh` exits zero on a fresh database; this is the terminal story and depends on every other story. |\n\n**Totals:** features: 10 · stories: 29\n\n## Surfaced Acceptance Criteria\n\n| ID | Story ID | Criterion |\n|---|---|---|\n| AC-001 | CLI-002 | Running `ledger` with no arguments writes the usage listing of every command to stderr and exits 2. |\n| AC-002 | CLI-003 | A report whose total sums to zero prints `0.00`, never `-0.00`. |\n| AC-003 | DB-001 | A `postgres://` or `postgresql://` `DATABASE_URL` exits 1 with a diagnostic stating that this build provides no PostgreSQL backend. |\n| AC-004 | DB-003 | If another connection holds the write lock, then the command exits 1 and changes nothing. |\n| AC-005 | LOAD-001 | A header-only accounts file loads zero rows, prints `accounts,0`, and exits 0. |\n| AC-006 | LOAD-001 | If a file header does not match the table columns in order, then the load exits 3 and stores nothing. |\n| AC-007 | LOAD-003 | A transactions file loads only after its accounts and categories exist; otherwise the load exits 3 and stores nothing. |\n| AC-008 | RPT-001 | With no accounts, `report balances` prints only `TOTAL,,0,0.00`. |\n| AC-009 | RPT-003 | With no transactions, `report monthly` prints only `TOTAL,0,0.00,0.00,0.00`. |\n| AC-010 | TXN-001 | Argument syntax is validated before any lookup, so a malformed amount exits 3 even when the account is absent. |\n| AC-011 | TXN-001 | A post to an account or category that does not exist exits 3, not 4. |\n| AC-012 | TXN-002 | A non-integer id argument to `txn get` exits 3 before any lookup. |\n| AC-013 | VAL-002 | An input amount of zero in any form (`0`, `0.00`, `-0.00`) exits 3. |\n| AC-014 | XFER-001 | A transfer naming an unknown account exits 3, not 4. |\n\n## Relationship Model\n\n| Source or group | Relationship type | Related source or group | Evidence | Delivery implication |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Commands and Exit codes tables | instruction-to-test | sources/run.sh checks A1–Z2 | Each command row and exit rule is exercised by named checks, for example `F6` for amount format and `D1` for atomic load | Each command story cites the run.sh checks it must satisfy |\n| sources/run.sh | test-kit-to-implementation | `ledger` executable at the application root | Every check invokes `\"$APP/ledger\"` | VER-002 gates the whole application |\n| sources/seed_accounts.csv, sources/seed_categories.csv, sources/seed_transactions.csv | dependency | sources/run.sh B1–B3 | run.sh reads these files from `$SEED`, which resolves to `sources/` | All four files are staged beside run.sh |\n| sources/seed_transactions_bad.csv | dependency | sources/run.sh D1 | Row 11 names unknown account `NOSUCH`, so the whole file is rejected | LOAD-003 must reject the whole file |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 1 | dependency | DB-003 | Every command is one transaction | DB-003 precedes every mutating story |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 2 | dependency | DB-004 | Balance rule applies to post, amend, delete, transfer, and load | DB-004 precedes TXN-001 through TXN-004, XFER-001, and LOAD-003 |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Database section | dependency | DB-001 | `DATABASE_URL` dispatch order | DB-001 precedes DB-002 and every data story |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 5 | dependency | VAL-002 | Amount format used by every report and mutating command | VAL-002 precedes RPT-001 through RPT-003 |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 7 | dependency | TXN-001 | Transfer ids are the next two after the current maximum | XFER-001 follows TXN-001 |\n| sources/run.sh F10 and G1 | dependency | TXN-001, XFER-001 | Id assignment after a deletion reuses the freed id; transfers take the following two | Id logic is one shared function |\n| SEA_TRIALS.md st-002 | dependency | VER-001 | `bin/test.sh` is the proof for the POSIX suite | VER-001 is the producer of the suite |\n\n## Source Roles\n\n| Path | Role | Plan disposition | Build disposition |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md | author intent | compass | prompt-only |\n| sources/run.sh | conformance harness | context | stage |\n| sources/seed_accounts.csv | asset | context | stage |\n| sources/seed_categories.csv | asset | context | stage |\n| sources/seed_transactions.csv | asset | context | stage |\n| sources/seed_transactions_bad.csv | asset | context | stage |\n\n## Planning Instructions\n\n### Delivery Shape\n\nThe system is a command-line program. Inputs are the `ledger` subcommand arguments, CSV files named on the command line, and the environment variables `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_PATH`. Outputs are CSV on standard output for successful commands, one diagnostic line on standard error for failures, an exit code from the table in the brief, and database state changed only by commands that succeed.\n\nThe persistence boundary is the single store module. Three tables are created by `init`: `accounts` (`account` primary key, `name`), `categories` (`category` primary key, `description`), and `transactions` (`txn_id` integer primary key, `date`, `account` referencing `accounts`, `category` referencing `categories`, `amount` integer cents, `memo`). Plan records the exact contract in `DATABASE.md`. Every command, including reports, reads and writes through that boundary.\n\nThe `bin/test.sh` wrapper is POSIX `sh` and runs pytest against a temporary SQLite database.\n\n### Story Realization Map\n\n| Story ID | Kind | Durable scope | Cited evidence | Related files |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| CLI-001 | capability | Dispatch, usage errors | INSTRUCTIONS Exit codes 2; run.sh U1, U2 | `ledger` entry |\n| CLI-002 | capability | Help text per command | Core baseline for cli; AC-001 | `ledger` entry, usage text |\n| CLI-003 | capability | Output writer | INSTRUCTIONS Output section | output module |\n| DB-001 | integration | Database URL resolution | INSTRUCTIONS Database section | store module |\n| DB-002 | capability | Error mapping to exit 1 | INSTRUCTIONS Exit codes 1 | store module |\n| DB-003 | capability | Command transaction wrapper | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 1 | store module |\n| DB-004 | capability | Balance check | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 2 | store module |\n| SCHEMA-001 | migration | Create and drop tables | run.sh A1, Z1 | `DATABASE.md`, store module |\n| SCHEMA-002 | capability | Row counts | run.sh A2, B4, D3, G6 | store module, count command |\n| VAL-001 | capability | Code, name, memo rules | INSTRUCTIONS Rules 3, 4 | validation module |\n| VAL-002 | capability | Amount parse and format | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 5; run.sh F6 | validation module, output module |\n| VAL-003 | capability | Date validation | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 6; run.sh F7 | validation module |\n| LOAD-001 | capability | Accounts load | run.sh B1, D2 | loader module |\n| LOAD-002 | capability | Categories load | run.sh B2 | loader module |\n| LOAD-003 | capability | Transactions load | run.sh B3, D1; seed_transactions_bad.csv | loader module |\n| ACCT-001 | capability | Account add | run.sh E1, E2 | account module |\n| ACCT-002 | capability | Account get | run.sh E3, E5, E8 | account module |\n| ACCT-003 | capability | Account rename | run.sh E4 | account module |\n| ACCT-004 | capability | Account delete | run.sh E6, E7, E8 | account module |\n| TXN-001 | capability | Transaction post and id rule | run.sh F1, F5, F6, F10, G3 | transaction module |\n| TXN-002 | capability | Transaction get | run.sh F2, F4, F9 | transaction module |\n| TXN-003 | capability | Transaction amend | run.sh F3, G4 | transaction module |\n| TXN-004 | capability | Transaction delete | run.sh F8, G5 | transaction module |\n| XFER-001 | capability | Two-row transfer | run.sh G1, G2 | transfer module |\n| RPT-001 | capability | Balances report | run.sh C1, H1 | report module |\n| RPT-002 | capability | Categories report | run.sh C2, H2 | report module |\n| RPT-003 | capability | Monthly report | run.sh C3, H3 | report module |\n| VER-001 | test harness | Automated suite and `bin/test.sh` | SEA_TRIALS st-002 | `bin/test.sh`, pytest tests |\n| VER-002 | acceptance contract | Terminal grader gate | SEA_TRIALS st-001 | `sources/run.sh` |\n\n### Test and Acceptance Strategy\n\nEach feature story runs only the pytest node ids it owns and declares `Suite: scoped`. VER-001 proves `bin/test.sh` by running it with a pytest selector, not the whole suite. VER-002 is the single terminal verification story. It depends on every other story and its acceptance assertion declares `Suite: full`, running `sh sources/run.sh` unfiltered with zero failures.\n\nSea Trials prove the project-wide criteria: st-001 is the grader command, st-002 is the `bin/test.sh` command, and the remaining criteria are proofs or judgments carried in SEA_TRIALS.md.\n\n### Sequencing and Dependencies\n\n1. DB-001, DB-002, DB-003, SCHEMA-001, SCHEMA-002, CLI-001, CLI-003\n2. VAL-001, VAL-002, VAL-003, CLI-002\n3. DB-004\n4. LOAD-001, LOAD-002, LOAD-003 (LOAD-003 after DB-004 and both reference tables)\n5. ACCT-001 through ACCT-004\n6. TXN-001 through TXN-004 (TXN-001 before XFER-001)\n7. XFER-001\n8. RPT-001 through RPT-003\n9. VER-001\n10. VER-002 (terminal, after every story above)\n\nExternal dependencies: Python 3.11 or newer, SQLite, pytest, uv, and ruff.\n\n### Source Conflicts and Gaps\n\nNo blockers or questionnaires are emitted under the unattended UAT policy. Each ambiguity is resolved below by the narrowest behavior consistent with the sources.\n\n- **Persistence library not supplied.** The brief names a \"shipped persistence library\" and a relational layer generated from `DATABASE.md`, but neither is in the sources. Resolution: Plan authors the store module and the generated layer under DB-001 through DB-004 and SCHEMA-001, governed by Rigging `persistence.md`.\n- **Amount \"never zero\".** Resolution: a zero input amount in any form exits 3 (AC-013).\n- **PostgreSQL DSN.** The brief defines the DSN prefix but builds over SQLite. Resolution: the prefix is recognized and fails with exit 1 (AC-003). No PostgreSQL behavior is acceptance-tested.\n- **Pytest versus POSIX `bin/test.sh`.** Resolution: `bin/test.sh` is a POSIX wrapper that runs pytest.\n- **Validation precedence.** Resolution: argument syntax (exit 3) is checked before lookups (exit 4), and unknown referenced accounts or categories exit 3 (AC-010, AC-011, AC-014).\n- **Non-integer ids.** Resolution: exit 3 (AC-012).\n- **Help text.** The brief does not define help output. Resolution: help text appears in the stderr usage diagnostic only; no help command is added (CLI-002, AC-001).\n- **Concurrency.** The sources say nothing about concurrent writers. Resolution: each command is one transaction; lock contention exits 1 with no change (DB-003, AC-004).\n- **Balance check scope.** Resolution: DB-004 checks every account touched by the command after its changes and before commit.\n- **Header-only and mismatched files.** Resolution: a header-only file loads zero rows (AC-005); a mismatched header exits 3 (AC-006).\n- **Relative database path.** Resolution: `data/app.db` resolves against the working directory.\n- **Authentication and sensitive data.** The sources state no auth model. BEGIN ARTIFACT ANALYSIS.md ===\n# Blueprint Analysis: drydock Layers Testing Uat Case\n\n## Commander Expectations\n\n- assert the product is a command-line cash ledger, delivered as an executable named `ledger` at the application root\n- assert every command either completes in full or changes nothing\n- assert every report is computed from the database and never embeds a known answer\n- assert the supplied `sources/run.sh` grader exits zero unmodified against the completed application\n- assert all database access goes through the shipped persistence library, selected by `DATABASE_URL`\n- assert amounts are stored as integer cents and printed with exactly two decimal places\n- assert no account balance ever goes negative\n- assert the application provides a POSIX `bin/test.sh` whose automated suite passes\n\n## Crew\n\n| Crew | Charge |\n|---|---|\n| Commander | Defines intent and decides what done means. |\n| Team Lead | Confirms epic completeness and stakeholder expectations. |\n| Planning Crew | Authors atomic specifications and the ordered Manifest. |\n| Shipyard Crew | Builds the tickets without synchronous Commander access. |\n\n## Story List\n\n### Feature: Command Line Interface\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| CLI-001 | Dispatch commands and reject usage errors | Unknown command, unknown table, unknown report, or wrong argument count exits 2 with one stderr line and nothing on stdout. |\n| CLI-002 | Provide per-command help text | Every command and sub-verb in the Commands table has one line of help text, printed in the usage diagnostic on stderr. |\n| CLI-003 | Emit the CSV success output contract | Every successful command except `init` writes a header row then data rows, comma-separated, unquoted, `\\n` endings, no trailing spaces; `init` writes nothing. |\n\n### Feature: Database Access\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| DB-001 | Resolve the database location | `DATABASE_URL`, then `DATABASE_PATH`, then `data/app.db` is used; an optional `sqlite://` prefix is accepted; a `postgres://` or `postgresql://` value is recognized and fails with exit 1 in this build. |\n| DB-002 | Report unreachable database, missing tables, or unreadable files | Database unreachable, tables missing for a non-`init` command, or an unreadable input file exits 1 with no change. |\n| DB-003 | Run every command in one database transaction | Each command runs in one transaction; any failure rolls back all changes; a write lock held by another connection exits 1 with no change. |\n| DB-004 | Enforce the non-negative balance rule before commit | Any command that would leave an account touched by its changes below zero exits 3 with no change. |\n\n### Feature: Schema Lifecycle\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| SCHEMA-001 | Initialize an empty schema | `ledger init` drops the three tables if present, recreates them empty, writes nothing, and exits 0. |\n| SCHEMA-002 | Count rows per table | `ledger count` prints `table,rows` then `accounts`, `categories`, `transactions` counts in that order. |\n\n### Feature: Field Validation\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| VAL-001 | Validate codes, names, descriptions, and memos | Codes are 1 to 12 characters of `A-Z` and `0-9`; names and descriptions are 1 to 40 characters; memos are 0 to 60; none contains a comma or newline; violations exit 3. |\n| VAL-002 | Parse and format amounts | Input matches `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`, is nonzero, and is stored as integer cents; output has two decimals, a leading `-` when negative, and no separators. |\n| VAL-003 | Validate calendar dates | Dates are real `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar dates; impossible dates such as `2026-02-30` exit 3. |\n\n### Feature: Bulk Loading\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| LOAD-001 | Load the accounts file | `load accounts <csv>` checks the header, validates each row, rejects duplicate keys, stores all or none, and prints `table,loaded` and `accounts,<rows>`. |\n| LOAD-002 | Load the categories file | `load categories <csv>` follows the same header, validation, duplicate, and atomicity contract as accounts. |\n| LOAD-003 | Load the transactions file | `load transactions <csv>` keeps each file `txn_id`, rejects unknown accounts or categories and any balance breach for the whole file, and stores none of the rows on rejection. |\n\n### Feature: Account Maintenance\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| ACCT-001 | Add an account | `account add` prints the new row with `0` transactions and `0.00` balance; a duplicate code exits 3. |\n| ACCT-002 | Get an account | `account get` prints the row with transaction count and balance; an absent code exits 4. |\n| ACCT-003 | Rename an account | `account rename` prints the updated row; an absent code exits 4; an invalid name exits 3. |\n| ACCT-004 | Delete an account | `account delete` prints `deleted` and the code when no transactions reference it; an in-use account exits 3; an absent account exits 4. |\n\n### Feature: Transaction Maintenance\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| TXN-001 | Post a transaction | `txn post` assigns the next id, validates all fields, checks that the account and category exist, applies the balance rule, and prints the new row. |\n| TXN-002 | Get a transaction | `txn get` prints the row; an absent id exits 4; a non-integer id exits 3. |\n| TXN-003 | Amend a transaction amount | `txn amend` changes only the amount, prints the updated row, applies the balance rule, and exits 4 for an absent id. |\n| TXN-004 | Delete a transaction | `txn delete` prints `deleted` and the id, applies the balance rule, and exits 4 for an absent id. |\n\n### Feature: Transfers\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| XFER-001 | Transfer between two accounts | `transfer` stores two `TRANSFER` rows with the next two ids and the stated memos, or neither; requires a positive amount, distinct accounts, and existing accounts; applies the balance rule. |\n\n### Feature: Reports\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| RPT-001 | Balances report | `report balances` prints one row per account ordered by code, then the `TOTAL` row. |\n| RPT-002 | Categories report | `report categories` prints every category ordered by code, including those with no transactions, then the `TOTAL` row. |\n| RPT-003 | Monthly report | `report monthly` prints one row per `YYYY-MM` that has transactions, ascending, then the `TOTAL` row. |\n\n### Feature: Verification and Acceptance\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| VER-001 | Provide the `bin/test.sh` automated suite | `bin/test.sh` is POSIX `sh`, drives the pytest suite against a real temporary database, and exits zero only when every test passes. |\n| VER-002 | Pass the supplied acceptance grader end to end | `sh sources/run.sh` exits zero on a fresh database; this is the terminal story and depends on every other story. |\n\n**Totals:** features: 10 · stories: 29\n\n## Surfaced Acceptance Criteria\n\n| ID | Story ID | Criterion |\n|---|---|---|\n| AC-001 | CLI-002 | Running `ledger` with no arguments writes the usage listing of every command to stderr and exits 2. |\n| AC-002 | CLI-003 | A report whose total sums to zero prints `0.00`, never `-0.00`. |\n| AC-003 | DB-001 | A `postgres://` or `postgresql://` `DATABASE_URL` exits 1 with a diagnostic stating that this build provides no PostgreSQL backend. |\n| AC-004 | DB-003 | If another connection holds the write lock, then the command exits 1 and changes nothing. |\n| AC-005 | LOAD-001 | A header-only accounts file loads zero rows, prints `accounts,0`, and exits 0. |\n| AC-006 | LOAD-001 | If a file header does not match the table columns in order, then the load exits 3 and stores nothing. |\n| AC-007 | LOAD-003 | A transactions file loads only after its accounts and categories exist; otherwise the load exits 3 and stores nothing. |\n| AC-008 | RPT-001 | With no accounts, `report balances` prints only `TOTAL,,0,0.00`. |\n| AC-009 | RPT-003 | With no transactions, `report monthly` prints only `TOTAL,0,0.00,0.00,0.00`. |\n| AC-010 | TXN-001 | Argument syntax is validated before any lookup, so a malformed amount exits 3 even when the account is absent. |\n| AC-011 | TXN-001 | A post to an account or category that does not exist exits 3, not 4. |\n| AC-012 | TXN-002 | A non-integer id argument to `txn get` exits 3 before any lookup. |\n| AC-013 | VAL-002 | An input amount of zero in any form (`0`, `0.00`, `-0.00`) exits 3. |\n| AC-014 | XFER-001 | A transfer naming an unknown account exits 3, not 4. |\n\n## Relationship Model\n\n| Source or group | Relationship type | Related source or group | Evidence | Delivery implication |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Commands and Exit codes tables | instruction-to-test | sources/run.sh checks A1–Z2 | Each command row and exit rule is sources/seed_transactions.csv | dependency | sources/run.sh B1–B3 | run.sh reads these files from `$SEED`, which resolves to `sources/` | All four files are staged beside run.sh |\n| sources/seed_transactions_bad.csv | dependency | sources/run.sh D1 | Row 11 names unknown account `NOSUCH`, so the whole file is rejected | LOAD-003 must reject the whole file |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 1 | dependency | DB-003 | Every command is one transaction | DB-003 precedes every mutating story |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 2 | dependency | DB-004 | Balance rule applies to post, amend, delete, transfer, and load | DB-004 precedes TXN-001 through TXN-004, XFER-001, and LOAD-003 |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Database section | dependency | DB-001 | `DATABASE_URL` dispatch order | DB-001 precedes DB-002 and every data story |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 5 | dependency | VAL-002 | Amount format used by every report and mutating command | VAL-002 precedes RPT-001 through RPT-003 |\n| sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md Rule 7 | dependency | TXN-001 | Transfer ids are the next two after the current maximum | XFER-001 follows TXN-001 |\n| sources/run.sh F10 and G1 | dependency | TXN-001, XFER-001 | Id assignment after a deletion reuses the freed id; transfers take the following two | Id logic is one shared function |\n| SEA_TRIALS.md Planning Instructions\n\n### Delivery Shape\n\nThe system is a command-line program. Inputs are the `ledger` subcommand arguments, CSV files named on the command line, and the environment variables `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_PATH`. Outputs are CSV on standard output for successful commands, one diagnostic line on standard error for failures, an exit code from the table in the brief, and database state changed only by commands that succeed.\n\nThe persistence boundary is the single store module. Three tables are created by `init`: `accounts` (`account` primary key, `name`), `categories` (`category` primary key, `description`), and `transactions` (`txn_id` integer primary key, `date`, `account` referencing `accounts`, `category` referencing `categories`, `amount` integer cents, `memo`). Plan records the exact contract in `DATABASE.md`. Every command, including reports, reads and writes through that boundary.\n\nThe `bin/test.sh` wrapper is POSIX `sh` and runs pytest against a temporary SQLite database.\n\n### Story Realization Map\n\n| Story ID | Kind | Durable scope | Cited evidence | Related files |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| CLI-001 | capability | Dispatch, usage errors | INSTRUCTIONS Exit codes 2; run.sh U1, U2 | `ledger` entry |\n| CLI-002 | capability | Help text per command | Core baseline for cli; AC-001 | `ledger` entry, usage text |\n| CLI-003 | capability | Output writer | INSTRUCTIONS Output section | output module |\n| DB-001 | integration | Database URL resolution | INSTRUCTIONS Database section | store module |\n| DB-002 | capability | Error mapping to exit 1 | INSTRUCTIONS Exit codes 1 | store module |\n| DB-003 | capability | Command transaction wrapper | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 1 | store module |\n| DB-004 | capability | Balance check | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 2 | store module |\n| SCHEMA-001 | migration | Create and drop tables | run.sh A1, Z1 | `DATABASE.md`, store module |\n| SCHEMA-002 | capability | Row counts | run.sh A2, B4, D3, G6 | store module, count command |\n| VAL-001 | capability | Code, name, memo rules | INSTRUCTIONS Rules 3, 4 | validation module |\n| VAL-002 | capability | Amount parse and format | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 5; run.sh F6 | validation module, output module |\n| VAL-003 | capability | Date validation | INSTRUCTIONS Rule 6; run.sh F7 | validation module |\n| LOAD-001 | capability | Accounts load | run.sh B1, D2 | loader module |\n| LOAD-002 | capability | Categories load | run.sh B2 | loader module |\n| LOAD-003 | capability | Transactions load | run.sh B3, D1; seed_transactions_bad.csv | loader module |\n| ACCT-001 | capability | Account add | run.sh E1, E2 | account module |\n| ACCT-002 | capability | Account get | run.sh E3, E5, E8 | account module |\n| ACCT-003 | capability | Account rename | run.sh E4 | account module |\n| ACCT-004 | capability | Account delete | run.sh E6, E7, E8 | account module |\n| TXN-001 | capability | Transaction post and id rule | run.sh F1, F5, F6, F10, G3 | transaction module |\n| TXN-002 | capability | Transaction get | run.sh F2, F4, F9 | transaction module |\n| TXN-003 | capability | Transaction amend | run.sh F3, G4 | transaction module |\n| TXN-004 | capability | Transaction delete | run.sh F8, G5 | transaction module |\n| XFER-001 | capability | Two-row transfer | run.sh G1, G2 | transfer module |\n| RPT-001 | capability | Balances report | run.sh C1, H1 | report module |\n| RPT-002 | capability | Categories report | run.sh C2, H2 | report module |\n| RPT-003 | capability | Monthly report | run.sh C3, H3 | report module |\n| VER-001 | test harness | Automated suite and `bin/test.sh` | SEA_TRIALS st-002 | `bin/test.sh`, pytest tests |\n| VER-002 | acceptance contract | Terminal grader gate | SEA_TRIALS st-001 | `sources/run.sh` |\n\n### Test and Acceptance Strategy\n\nEach feature story runs only the pytest node ids it owns and declares `Suite: scoped`. VER-001 proves `bin/test.sh` by running it with a pytest selector, not the whole suite. VER-002 is the single terminal verification story. It depends on every other story and its acceptance assertion declares `Suite: full`, running `sh sources/run.sh` unfiltered with zero failures.\n\nSea Trials prove the project-wide criteria: st-001 is the grader command, st-002 is the `bin/test.sh` command, and the remaining criteria are proofs or judgments carried in SEA_TRIALS.md.\n\n### Sequencing and Dependencies\n\n1. DB-001, DB-002, DB-003, SCHEMA-001, SCHEMA-002, CLI-001, CLI-003\n2. VAL-001, VAL-002, VAL-003, CLI-002\n3. DB-004\n4. LOAD-001, LOAD-002, LOAD-003 (LOAD-003 after DB-004 and both reference tables)\n5. ACCT-001 through ACCT-004\n6. TXN-001 through TXN-004 (TXN-001 before XFER-001)\n7. XFER-001\n8. RPT-001 through RPT-003\n9. VER-001\n10. VER-002 (terminal, after every story above)\n\nExternal dependencies: Python 3.11 or newer, SQLite, pytest, uv, and ruff.\n\n### Source Conflicts and Gaps\n\nNo blockers or questionnaires are emitted under the unattended UAT policy. Each ambiguity is resolved below by the narrowest behavior consistent with the sources.\n\n- **Persistence library not supplied.** The brief names a \"shipped persistence library\" and a relational layer generated from `DATABASE.md`, but neither is in the sources. Resolution: Plan authors the store module and the generated layer under DB-001 through DB-004 and SCHEMA-001, governed by Rigging `persistence.md`.\n- **Amount \"never zero\".** Resolution: a zero input amount in any form exits 3 (AC-013).\n- **PostgreSQL DSN.** The brief defines the DSN prefix but builds over SQLite. Resolution: the prefix is recognized and fails with exit 1 (AC-003).
